name: tokenizer-lab
desc: Free, open-source tokenizer playground for Windows — tokenize text like any GGUF model, count tokens, compare two. 100 MB offline MIT.
features: ✅ **Loads real tokenizers** — reads tokenizer config from GGUF headers or Hugging Face folders, no approximations
✅ **Color token view** — text broken into tokens with boundary markers so odd splits are visible instantly
✅ **Token and cost count** — character, word and token totals with a per-million-token cost field
✅ **Two-tokenizer compare** — same text side by side across two models to see who wastes context
✅ **Special token map** — BOS, EOS and control tokens listed with their ids and rendered forms
✅ **File batch mode** — drop a folder of texts and get a token-count table for every file
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and tokenizer backend bundled, portable, offline, MIT
compare: | Feature | **tokenizer-lab** | tiktoken web | HF tokenizers | Online counters |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Free web | Free, OSS | Free web |
| Reads GGUF tokenizer config | **Yes** | No | No | No |
| Folder batch counting | **Yes** | No | Scripted | No
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Browser | Python env | Browser
faqQ: how many tokens is my text? count tokens for local LLM models
faqA: Online counters usually run one public tokenizer, so counts drift on Llama or Mistral vocabularies by double digits. tokenizer-lab reads the actual tokenizer config out of your GGUF file and counts with it. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline — drop a folder in and compare models side by side.
s1: Dark token view (#121418, orange #FB923C): text pane with colored token blocks, count bar reading 187 tokens and 412 characters, tokenizer dropdown showing Llama-3.
s2: Compare mode: two columns tokenizing the same paragraph, counts 187 versus 203 highlighted, delta chip reading 8 percent fewer tokens on the left.
s3: Special token table: BOS and EOS rows with ids, rendered forms and byte notes, filter field, footer chip reading tokenizer loaded from model.gguf.
